small_guidance:
- The current kernel calls `self.conv(x)` then a custom epilogue — conv dominates. Tuning the pool/sigmoid/sum tail won't help much. If staying small, at least make the kernel 2D-grid `(N, OC)` so each program handles one (n, oc) plane and reduce a per-(n) atomic_add or partial buffer to remove the serial OC loop.
- Add larger BLOCK_P (2048) with num_warps=8, num_stages=3 to the autotune list, and key on PH*PW so the right tile is chosen for the 96x96 pooled grid.
- Drop the `conv_out.contiguous()` after channels_last conv — it forces a layout copy of a 128*64*382*382 tensor; instead make the fused kernel index strided NHWC directly.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton conv kernel (im2col-style implicit GEMM) that fuses the 4x4 avg-pool, sigmoid, and per-batch sum in the epilogue. Conv2d on (128, 8, 384, 384) -> (128, 64, 382, 382) is the runtime bottleneck (~13ms baseline already includes it; the current kernel spends most time in cuDNN + a layout flip). Output the pooled (N, 64, 95, 95) only — or even just the per-N scalar — so the (N,64,382,382) tensor never materializes.
- Strategy: one program per (n, oc_tile, pooled_tile). Inner loop is GEMM-K over (IC * KH * KW = 72). Accumulate the conv output for a 4x4 pool window in registers (16 spatial positions per pooled output), apply mean, sigmoid, and reduce across pooled positions and oc into a per-n partial that is atomically added into out[n]. This avoids ever writing the conv result to global memory — the dominant memory traffic today.
- Use channels_last input layout so the K-loop over IC is contiguous; KH*KW=9 and IC=8 fit nicely as a K=72 inner reduction. Tile BLOCK_OC=64 (full), BLOCK_P=16 or 32 pooled outputs per program. Fold sigmoid + sum into the epilogue (closed form `1/(1+exp(-x))`), and use `tl.atomic_add` on `out[n]` per program.
